newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt to seek more EU structural funds - Bruton.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt to seek more EU structural funds - Bruton.

text.p: Irish prime minister John Bruton told parliament on Tuesday that his government would be seeking substantial funds in the next allocation of structural funds from the European Union.
"Ireland will be making a case to retain its Objective 1 status for those funds," he said.

He cited the need to develop internal transport and the fact that Ireland was the only part of the EU without surface links to the other member states as reasons why it should get favourable consideration.
Bruton called on the EU to take account of Ireland's real income, as shown by GNP figures, and not its theoretical income, as shown by GDP.
There was a 12.5 percent difference between those two measurements of the national income, he said.
